bug_semantics: NIOHTTP1's HTTPDecoder accumulates every HTTP/1 header field into an unbounded [(String,String)] (then HTTPHeaders) before any application handler runs. After the llhttp switch the decoder enforced only an 80 KB cap on a single field name/value (currentFieldByteLength, reset in finish() per field). There was no running total of header-block bytes and no field-count cap, so a remote peer could send hundreds of thousands of small valid headers on one request/response and exhaust memory (or crash consumers that bridge into swift-http-types HTTPFields). Attack path: unauthenticated HTTP/1 bytes -> BetterHTTPParser on_header_field/on_header_value -> HTTPDecoder.didReceiveHeaderValue headers.append -> HTTPServerRequestPart.head / HTTPClientResponsePart.head. Fixed in 2.100.0 by NIOHTTPDecoderLimitConfiguration (maxHeaderFieldSize 80 KB, maxHeaderListSize 2 MB, maxHeaderFieldCount 256) rejecting overflow with HTTPParserError.headerOverflow.
flaw_origin: Until 2.41.1 the bundled nodejs http_parser enforced HTTP_MAX_HEADER_SIZE (80 KB) as a per-message nread total (COUNT_HEADER_SIZE -> HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW), which NIO mapped to HTTPParserError.headerOverflow. PR #2263 replaced that parser with llhttp. Member c154ceec1ef7880be2559b3512c4f5761c527e03 rewired HTTPDecoder to c_nio_llhttp_execute and deleted the HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW mapping; the vendored llhttp had no equivalent total-header cap. A later member, 75997b7ad9be2780fcb168727eb870c2463b20dc, restored only a per-field 80 KB check. Those members were squash-landed on main as 6918034260d1b0ff46a24a6e3ced445bc2d0ed4b (first released in 2.42.0). The many-small-headers DoS is the missing total/count bounds, not a new append site.

Pre-llhttp total cap at tag 2.41.1: Sources/CNIOHTTPParser/include/c_nio_http_parser.h:68 `# define HTTP_MAX_HEADER_SIZE (80*1024)` and c_nio_http_parser.c COUNT_HEADER_SIZE increments nread across the header block and SET_ERRNO(HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW) when nread > max_header_size. HTTPDecoder mapped HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW -> HTTPParserError.headerOverflow.

Parent of BIC 1b16631ac4e9e895c2f8c7a298d8c177241549ab HTTPDecoder.swift still calls c_nio_http_parser_execute_swift (line 361) / c_nio_http_parser_execute (line 366) and still has `case HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW:` (line 740). No c_nio_llhttp_execute, no maximumHeaderFieldSize, no validateHeaderLength. Vulnerable llhttp decode path is absent in that parent tree.

BIC member https://github.com/apple/swift-nio/commit/c154ceec1ef7880be2559b3512c4f5761c527e03 (PR #2263 'Update to correctly use LLHTTP'): HTTPDecoder.swift switches to c_nio_llhttp_execute (line 376), drops the HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW mapping (replaced by HPE_INTERNAL at line 775), and still does unbounded `self.headers.append` in didReceiveHeaderValue (line 570). git grep of that tree's Sources/CNIOLLHTTP found no HTTP_MAX_HEADER_SIZE / max_header_size / HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW.

Follow-on member https://github.com/apple/swift-nio/commit/75997b7ad9be2780fcb168727eb870c2463b20dc ('Add back the policing of length fields that llhttp removed') introduces private static let maximumHeaderFieldSize = 80 * 1024 and validateHeaderLength on currentFieldByteLength, which finish() resets per field — a per-field cap, not the old per-message nread total.

Fix b24872d3aa4a4d31057a922e72db0c04c8e909be 'Merge commit from fork' / 'Add configurable HTTP/1 decoder parsing limits', single parent 87f935b70c5ed41e45d7e3be3cd39f122d872da3. Adds NIOHTTPDecoderLimitConfiguration (maxHeaderListSize = 16384*128 = 2 MB, maxHeaderFieldCount = 256) and BetterHTTPParser totalHeadersByteLength / field-count checks that set HTTPParserError.headerOverflow (HTTPDecoder.swift ~398-399, 550-558). merge-base --is-ancestor b24872d3 2.99.0 -> false; 2.100.0 -> true (name-rev tags/2.100.0~1). Private-fork members are not in public history, so this is both fix_sha and direct_fix_sha.

Maintainer confirmation of lost total cap: apple/swift-nio#3608 (weissi, after 2.100.0) states the HTTP parser silently changed the default header buffer size from 80 kB (old limit that was unfortunately lost) to 2 MB.

reasoning: The advisory is a real CWE-770/CWE-400 DoS: HTTP/1 header fields are appended into HTTPHeaders with no cumulative size or count bound, so one unauthenticated peer can inflate memory or crash HTTPFields bridges. GitHub GHSA-rj37-6j9x-74q6 is published (withdrawn_at null). MITRE cveawg has no CVE-2026-28980 JSON record, but the vendor GHSA and Swift forums assign that CVE and do not reject the issue, so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. The original 2017 decoder already appended headers in Swift, but nodejs http_parser's 80 KB per-message nread cap made unbounded many-small-headers impossible; that is not this CVE. git log -S / parent-tree inspection show the total cap disappeared when PR #2263 moved NIO onto llhttp. The squash 69180342 is not the BIC. Public member c154ceec is the smallest commit that first wrote the working decoder path that executes llhttp and no longer maps/enforces HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW; its parent 1b16631 still feeds http_parser and still has the overflow case. Member 75997b7a then wrote the insufficient per-field-only 80 KB check that matches the advisory's pre-patch description; it is a follow-on, not the first write of unbounded totals. The squash is first contained in 2.42.0 (so the GHSA '<2.100.0' range is wider than the true start, but 2.99.0 is affected and 2.100.0 carries the fix). AI is judged only from the BIC commit object: human SwiftNIO maintainer Cory Benfield, no AI authorship/co-authorship trailers. Verdict NOT_AI.
